chain.label: Air Midwest/FAA failed to oversee HTS maintenance station practices
chain.trigger: Air Midwest did not adequately oversee the work performed by RALLC and SMART personnel at its HTS maintenance station

chain.label: Mechanic had never rigged a Beech 1900D elevator system and lacked D6 training
chain.trigger: Neither mechanic had previously performed the complete D6 check.

caused_by.evidence: none of the seven maintenance personnel who were on duty at HTS on the night of January 6, 2003, were Air Midwest employees

chain.label: QA inspector gave inadequate OJT/supervision during the elevator cable work
chain.trigger: the RALLC quality assurance inspector did not provide adequate OJT and supervision to the SMART mechanic who examined and incorrectly adjusted the elevator control system

caused_by.evidence: the mechanic needed more training and supervision than the quality assurance inspector had provided

chain.label: Mechanic skipped required rigging-procedure steps while adjusting cable tension, with inspector's concurrence
chain.trigger: the mechanic bypassed several steps of the complete elevator control system rigging procedure...he and the quality assurance inspector discussed which steps to bypass

caused_by.evidence: the quality assurance inspector...left the mechanic unsupervised during the elevator control cable inspections and turnbuckle adjustments

chain.label: Elevator control system misrigged, restricting downward travel to ~7° AND (about half normal)
chain.trigger: the incorrect rigging restricted the airplane's elevator travel to 7º AND, or about one-half of the downward travel specified by the airplane manufacturer

caused_by.evidence: adjustments to the cable turnbuckles during maintenance resulted in FDR pitch control measurements that showed a 9º AND loss of travel

chain.label: Postmaintenance functional check failed to detect the elevator misrig
chain.trigger: the postmaintenance checks performed by the quality assurance inspector and the mechanic were not adequate to detect the elevator control system misrig

caused_by.evidence: the RALLC quality assurance inspector's failure to detect the incorrect rigging of the elevator control system

chain.label: Air Midwest's FAA-approved average weight/balance program understated actual passenger and baggage weights
chain.trigger: Air Midwest's weight and balance program at the time of the accident was not correct and resulted in a substantially inaccurate weight and balance calculation for flight 5481

chain.label: Actual weight (~17,700 lb) and CG (~45.5% MAC) exceeded certified aft CG limit of 40% MAC
chain.trigger: the accident airplane had an actual weight of 17,700 ±200 pounds and an actual CG position of 45.5 ±2 percent MAC

caused_by.evidence: Air Midwest's weight and balance program... resulted in a substantially inaccurate weight and balance calculation for flight 5481

chain.label: Airplane pitched up uncontrollably on rotation; full forward control input could not overcome the nose-up moment
chain.trigger: the airplane's loss of pitch control during takeoff resulted from the incorrect rigging of the elevator control system compounded by the airplane's aft center of gravity

caused_by.evidence: about 9º to 10º AND elevator was required to establish a controlled climb at the accident airplane's actual weight and CG position
flight 5481 had an excessive aft CG, which, combined with the reduced downward elevator travel...rendered the airplane uncontrollable in the pitch axis

chain.label: Airplane pitched to 54° ANU, airspeed decayed to 31 knots, stall warning sounded, and violent roll excursions followed
chain.trigger: the FDR recorded a maximum pitch attitude of 54º ANU...a maximum left roll of 127º and a minimum airspeed of 31 knots

caused_by.evidence: the beginning of a sound similar to the stall warning horn

chain.label: Airplane struck a US Airways maintenance hangar and crashed on airport property
chain.trigger: The airplane struck a US Airways maintenance hangar located on CLT property

caused_by.evidence: the FDR recorded a maximum right roll of 68º and a maximum vertical acceleration of 1.9 Gs...The airplane struck a US Airways maintenance hangar

chain.label: 21 killed (2 crew, 19 passengers) and 1 minor ground injury; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The 2 flight crewmembers and 19 passengers aboard the airplane were killed, 1 person on the ground received minor injuries, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire
